items.note: Two-group experiment in which 64 design students did a three-hour walking-cane design task with AIGC tools (ChatGPT, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion) or traditional software; rated creative performance was higher with AIGC (d = 0.55); the abstract does not say how students were assigned.

System paper with a within-subject study (N = 14) comparing the NexusAI LLM diagramming system with a baseline (AI-configuration comparison likely) on design-space exploration and fixation; below 50 participants, and it is unclear whether the outputs are scored for creativity.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, publisher page failed); search notes describe a quasi-experiment over four task rounds comparing a GenAI multi-agent system with a single-agent model for undergraduates' creative problem solving; N and the creativity measure are unknown.

Fashion pattern design experiment in which AI style transfer extended human-originated concepts, and experts rated the AI-extended designs as more creative than the human-originated ones; it is unclear whether participants differ in AI access or whether this is a comparison of designs before and after AI extension (possibly ai_vs_human), so the full text should decide.

Two online experiments compare product ideas from humans, GPT-4, and co-creation modes (human ideas revised with GPT) on quality and diversity rated by humans and deep-learning measures; it mixes an AI-versus-human comparison with a human-with-AI condition, and the abstract does not state assignment or N (SSRN version).

Comparative quasi-experiment in which college design students used ChatGPT-4 or DeepSeek (and, apparently, conventional creative methods) for personalised learning; outcomes are AI-assisted design performance, creative self-efficacy, and engagement; N is not stated, and it is unclear whether design performance is a creativity score.

Sixty university students randomly assigned to create digital stories with GAI tools (ChatGPT, Midjourney, Runway) or traditional methods over 20 weeks; team creativity performance (novelty, user experience) was higher with GAI, but the abstract says outcomes were assessed with pre/post surveys, so the creativity measure may be self-reported; teams, not individuals, may be the unit.

Mixed-methods study in which 47 participants did analysis and synthesis writing tasks with or without AI assistance, measuring textual overlap between AI suggestions and their writing, plus a think-aloud (n = 4) of a reflective interface; the outcome is reuse of AI text rather than creativity or cross-writer diversity, and N is below 50 (arXiv 2605.15322 is the same work).

System paper with a within-subjects study (N = 24) on a poster image creation task comparing the HAICo divergent/convergent co-creation system with ChatGPT (AI-configuration comparison); HAICo outperformed on creativity dimensions, but it is unclear whether these are rated outputs or self-reports; below 50 participants.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar had none); search notes describe a field experiment in which employers were randomly offered AI-written first drafts of job posts, which made posts more generic and less informative; the task (job-post writing) is at the edge of the creativity scope, and genericness may count as a homogenization outcome.
